faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's net banking portal using the ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility, or through your stockbroker's platform. Your money remains blocked in your account until allotment.
The lot size is the minimum number of shares you must apply for in an IPO. You cannot apply for fewer than this number, and you must apply in multiples of the lot size.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mainboard and SME IPOs?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger, more established companies that list on the main exchanges (NSE, BSE). SME (Small and Medium Enterprise) IPOs are for smaller companies that list on dedicated SME platforms (like NSE Emerge or BSE SME) with different, often less stringent, regulations.

faq.q: Can I apply for more than one lot?
faq.a: Yes, you can apply for multiple lots. However, for retail investors, the total application value cannot exceed ₹2 lakhs. If you apply for more than ₹2 lakhs, you fall into the HNI/NII category, which has different allotment rules.

faq.q: What happens if I don't get an allotment?
faq.a: If you are not allotted any shares, the money that was blocked in your bank account for the IPO application will be unblocked and available for use, usually within a few days after the allotment date.
